source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Reduce nursing participation in decisions so interprofessional care can be streamlined around the authority of a single profession.","B":"Eliminate professional role distinctions so all clinicians perform the same tasks and hold the same responsibilities.","C":"Promote mutual respect, shared information, and collaborative decision-making while preserving distinct professional roles.","D":"Limit communication across disciplines to formal orders, because shared planning increases ambiguity in patient care."}}
source_row.rationale: Effective interprofessional collaboration uses shared goals, explicit roles, open information exchange, mutual respect/support and coordinated decision-making rather than suppressing one discipline's input.
source_row.source_detail: TeamSTEPPS team/leadership tools emphasize shared plan, clear roles/responsibilities, information sharing, mutual support, briefs/huddles/debriefs and coordinated team performance. Current AHRQ TeamSTEPPS 3.0 curriculum rechecked 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.
source_row.stem: Which behavior best reflects effective interprofessional team leadership in a hospital?
